label: copy phase: outputting x/i/h/l, strongest when the next output is also from {x,i,h,l,1,0,c}
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase unit (99% of activation mass is in the copy phase; nearly silent in the original phase and at <DEL>). It is selective for the token being output: steps that output x, i, h or l carry about 92% of the activation mass (rate 12-14%, versus under 3% for every other output token; 1, v and d are weakly active). Within those steps it is gated further by the upcoming output: when the next output is also one of x/i/h/l/1/0/c, precision goes from 0.15 to 0.43, but this captures only about 59% of the mass. The rate peaks at recall positions 2-3 (early in the copy, but not recall 0-1) and drops on the last output step. It does not fire on outputs such as m, 3, 0, s, c, or on the first copy step. Precision stays low with every predicate tried (at most about 0.43), so the description is incomplete: most steps that output x/i/h/l do not activate it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: x, i, h, l, 1, v; least: k, t, a, q) and the next token to output (most: l, h, x, i, 1, 0; least: r, p, t, k); timing cues that raise it most: t=1, t=2, t=3.
